questions.question: When turning right out of a side road onto a main road, who must you give way to?
options: Traffic coming from both right and left
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 172 requires checking and giving way to both directions when turning right.

questions.question: Before moving back to the left lane after overtaking, what must you be sure of?
options: There is plenty of room ahead of the passed vehicle
The car behind flashes its lights
You are going at least 70 mph
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 133 warns not to cut in front of the vehicle you overtook.

questions.question: When approaching a roundabout, which side should you look to first for circulating traffic?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 tells you to give way to traffic coming from your right.

questions.question: If you are taking the third exit, when do you switch to a left exit signal?
options: Just after passing the second exit
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 times the left signal right after passing the exit before yours.

questions.question: In which direction do all roundabouts flow in Great Britain?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 and Rule 186 require clockwise travel on UK roundabouts.

questions.question: On a two-lane roundabout, where should you position your car?
options: Centred cleanly inside your marked lane
Hugging the grass island on every exit
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 tells drivers to keep cleanly within their lane markings.

questions.question: When taking the first exit on the left at a roundabout, which lane do you choose?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 says to approach in the left-hand lane for the first exit.

questions.question: As you approach a Give Way line, what should you do?
options: Slow down early so you can stop if traffic is coming
Keep your speed until the last metre
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 172 tells drivers to approach under control ready to give way.

questions.question: When a lane ahead is closed by cones, when should you merge?
options: Early and smoothly when you see a safe gap
At the very last cone by forcing in
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 133 advises changing lanes smoothly in good time.

questions.question: Does an entering car have priority over a car already on the roundabout?
options: No, traffic already on the roundabout from the right has priority
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 gives priority to circulating traffic from the right.

questions.question: Where should the central island of a UK roundabout always stay?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 keeps the central island on your right as you travel clockwise.

questions.question: If another car is circulating alongside you in the next lane, what must you avoid?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 warns against drifting into another lane on roundabouts.

questions.question: Where can you check which lane leads to your exit before reaching a busy roundabout?
options: Advance signs and painted arrows on the road
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 tells drivers to read signs and road markings early.

questions.question: What should you do if you miss your exit on a roundabout?
options: Stay on and go clockwise all the way around again
Stop and reverse back to the exit
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 says never reverse or turn back; simply go around clockwise.

questions.question: What do dashed white spiral lines on a large roundabout show?
options: Which lane path to follow to reach your exit
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 uses lane markings to guide traffic smoothly around large roundabouts.

questions.question: When taking the third exit to the right at a two-lane roundabout, which lane is usual?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 uses the right-hand lane for exits to the right unless signed otherwise.

questions.question: What do the white zig-zag lines beside a pedestrian crossing mean?
options: You must not park or overtake there
You may park for five minutes
You must speed up past the crossing
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 forbids parking and overtaking within crossing zig-zag lines.

questions.question: When may you enter a yellow criss-cross box junction to go straight ahead?
options: Whenever the traffic lights are green
Only when your exit road is clear
When the car ahead is still moving slowly
At any time if you signal
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 174 states you must not enter a box junction unless your exit is clear.

questions.question: At speeds up to 30 mph, how much side space should you leave when overtaking a cyclist?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 163 says to leave at least 1.5 metres when overtaking cyclists up to 30 mph.

questions.question: What minimum gap should you leave behind the car in front on a dry road?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 sets at least a two-second gap in dry conditions.

questions.question: Why could a late signal confuse other road users?
options: It gives them too little time to react safely
It breaks the speed limit rule
It turns off your brake lights
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 103 stresses signalling early enough for others to read and react.

questions.question: Can you drive above the speed limit briefly while overtaking?
options: Yes, for up to five seconds
No, you must never exceed the speed limit
Yes, if no cameras are nearby
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 makes clear that speed limits are the legal maximum at all times.

questions.question: If you want to turn into a side road just past a parked car, when do you signal left?
options: After passing the parked car so nobody thinks you are stopping
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 103 warns that early signals near parked cars can mislead others.

questions.question: What does a round white sign with a black diagonal stripe mean?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 links the national speed limit sign to 60 or 70 mph limits.

questions.question: What if a bus stops just before a zebra crossing to let someone cross? May you pass the bus?
options: No, you must wait behind the bus
Yes, pass slowly on the right
Yes, if you sound your horn
Only if no stripes are visible
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 bans passing the lead vehicle because it can hide pedestrians.

questions.question: You are turning right at a box junction. Your exit road is clear, but oncoming cars block your turn. May you wait in the box?
options: Yes, you may wait in the box to turn right
Only if you turn on hazard lights
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 174 makes a specific exception when turning right and waiting for oncoming traffic.

questions.question: If a large lorry is in front of you, why should you stay well back?
options: So you can see past it and its driver can see you in their mirrors
To stay in its blind spot
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 helps you stay visible and see further ahead.

questions.question: Before turning left soon after passing a cyclist, what must you check?
options: Do not overtake and immediately cut across the cyclist's path
Always turn sharply in front of them
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 163 and Rule 182 warn against 'left hooks' across cyclists.

questions.question: If your indicator bulb fails before a drive, what should you do?
options: Fix it before driving, or use clear arm signals if safe
Use hazard lights for every turn
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 103 includes arm signals when indicators are not working.

questions.question: When you see temporary orange or red 50 mph roadworks signs, what is the legal limit?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 applies to temporary mandatory speed limits at roadworks.

questions.question: You are approaching a crossing and see a cyclist ahead inside the zig-zag lines. What should you do?
options: Hold back behind the cyclist until past the crossing
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 forbids overtaking any vehicle inside the zig-zag zone.

questions.question: You are turning right at a box junction, and the road you want to turn into is jammed full. May you enter the box?
options: No, because your exit road is blocked
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 174 only allows waiting in the box if your exit road itself is clear.

questions.question: Who else needs similar wide clearance and slow passing speeds under Rule 163 / 215?
options: Horse riders and pedestrians walking in the road
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 163 gives wide, slow clearance to cyclists, horse riders, and walkers.

questions.question: When you stop in a queue behind another car, how much space should you leave?
options: Enough to see their rear tyres on the road
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 and queueing advice keep space to steer around if needed.

questions.question: Why should you also glance left and ahead as you pull onto a roundabout?
options: Traffic ahead may stop suddenly or a pedestrian may cross
Nothing can be ahead of you
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 checks both circulating traffic from the right and hazards ahead.

questions.question: When two lanes merge into one, how should you treat a driver alongside you?
options: Leave space and merge in turn safely
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 133 and merging advice promote safe, courteous lane changes.

questions.question: When pulling away from the side of the road, when should you signal?
options: Before you pull away, if other road users could benefit
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 103 advises signalling in good time when pulling away.

questions.question: Why should you often drive slower than the speed limit?
options: Roadworks, rain, bends, or parked cars can make the limit unsafe
Because speed limits are just suggestions
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 and 125 state the limit is a maximum, not a target.

questions.question: If the traffic light is green but the exit past the box is full, what could happen if you enter?
options: You will be stuck in the box when the cross traffic gets a green light
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 174 prevents drivers getting trapped across live junctions.

questions.question: What phrase helps drivers count two seconds cleanly?
options: Say 'Only a fool breaks the two-second rule'
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 suggests a steady two-second count past a fixed landmark.

questions.question: What if the first exit is straight ahead and there is no left turn?
options: Treat it as straight ahead and do not signal on approach unless signs show left
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 matches your signal to the road layout and signs.

questions.question: At a tiny mini-roundabout with little space, should you still signal your turn?
options: Yes, signal clearly in good time before entering
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 and 188 still require clear approach signals at mini-roundabouts.

questions.question: You are in the right-hand lane of a two-lane roundabout and want to exit. What must you check before signalling left and moving out?
options: Your left mirror and blind spot for vehicles on your left
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 requires checking left before moving across to exit.

questions.question: Why is a right signal on approach helpful to drivers waiting at the left-hand entrance?
options: It warns them you are staying on the roundabout past their exit
It tells them to pull out in front of you
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 helps waiting drivers judge whether you will cross their path.

questions.question: You see a car approaching from the right with its left indicator on. What should you do?
options: Wait until you are sure it is actually turning before pulling out
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 172 warns never to assume a flashing indicator means the driver will turn.

questions.question: If a main road has two lanes in one direction and you turn left onto it, which lane should you join?
options: The left-hand lane unless road signs say otherwise
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 172 and lane rules keep turning traffic in the left lane when clear.

questions.question: Why are zig-zag lines painted on BOTH the approach and exit sides of a crossing?
options: To keep views clear in both directions and stop overtaking or parking near the stripes
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 keeps both sides of the crossing clear for pedestrians and drivers.

questions.question: On a 50 mph rural road, why is 1.5 metres often not enough when passing a cyclist?
options: High speed creates strong air turbulence, so give even more room
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 163 explicitly requires even more space at speeds over 30 mph.

questions.question: You see a motorcycle filtering between lanes as you plan to move right. What should you do?
options: Steer right anyway because you are bigger
Hold your lane and wait until the rider has passed safely
Open your door to warn them
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 133 requires watching for motorcyclists before changing lanes.

questions.question: At a mini-roundabout, three cars arrive at once and nobody has clear priority. What should you do?
options: Make eye contact, proceed slowly, and give way if unsure
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 and courtesy advice help resolve deadlocks safely.
